why: Dependency direction: 18 generic KLS modules depend on the KLS target proposition KLS/Statement.lean (KLS.Conjecture): KLS/LogConcave/Isotropic.lean and KLS/LogConcave/HminusOneApproximation.lean import it directly and 16 further modules (LogConcave/{Stein,HessianStein,ConditionalFiber,IsotropicReduction}, LogConcave/Line/*, LogConcave/Density/GaussianSmoothing/*, LogConcave/Regular/Poincare, Geometry/Cheeger/Comparison) depend on it through LogConcave/Isotropic. A path-only move would make a generic family import the KLS-specific target statement.

Cycle check of the full split (survey option A-i-top, 140 moves): no module cycle, but a new root-level KLS<->LogConcave directory mutual pair (plus Geometry<->LogConcave and Cheeger<->Perimeter relocated); the Probability/ variant adds Poincare<->Probability, KLS<->Probability and Geometry<->Probability (33 pairs).

KLS/Geometry and KLS/LogConcave import each other (Geometry->LogConcave 7 edges, LogConcave->Geometry 4), so they could only move together; a clean move needs declaration-level splits of LogConcave/Isotropic.lean, LogConcave/HminusOneApproximation.lean and Geometry/Cheeger/Comparison.lean, which is an API/content migration, not path-only.

The rules already treat these directories as KLS-level object families: research/naming.md cites KLS/{ConditionalFiber,...}/ as a family example, and KLS/README.md places log-concave properties in LogConcave/ with target contracts and shared KLS objects at the KLS level. No per-paper import exists in them (0 direct and 0 transitive imports of KLS/{BKL,CEK,Klartag,Letwin}), so the naming.md dependency rule is satisfied in place.
